name: Adapt or Anchor — Vossberg's Convergence Pivot
description: A four-round, advanced strategy simulation set inside Vossberg Mess- und Regeltechnik AG, a EUR 720M industrial-instrumentation business unit of a German engineering group in Stuttgart (3,100 staff, 16% EBIT margin ≈ EUR 115M, 84% of revenue anchored in a converging hardware core). Software-native rivals now bundle commodity sensors with subscription analytics at 60–75% gross margin while Vossberg's hardware margin (38%) erodes 2–3 points a year. On 21 April 2026 Vossberg loses its largest water-utility account (EUR 43M, 6% of revenue, a reference customer) — not on price or quality, but to an integrated sensor-plus-predictive-analytics subscription it cannot match. The group CEO gives the business-unit head two quarters and a EUR 60M two-year envelope to present an adaptation plan. Playing the BU head, you (1) read the convergence — diagnose where value is migrating (from commoditising sensors to the analytics/subscription layer), how fast the threat moves, and how much of today's EBIT is borrowed time on a lagging installed base; (2) set the explore-exploit allocation of the EUR 60M across exploit levers (hardware cost-down, margin defence, calibration-service growth) and explore levers (analytics platform, software acquisition, partner/white-label, software talent), pricing each bet's payoff, horizon and risk; (3) redesign the reporting lines — integrate Digital Ventures inside the hardware P&L, separate it into an ambidextrous unit with its own P&L and incentives, or hybridise with shared platform and sales force — and decide what the venture shares with the core and what it must not; and (4) time the pivot — set the pace of the revenue shift, the staged investment gates, and respond to a rival's acquisition that accelerates convergence, defending the plan to the board. Grounded in Nils Stieglitz's research on strategic adaptation in converging industries: structure decides whether exploration survives the gravitational pull of the core. The math rewards a balanced allocation, an ambidextrous-with-shared-assets structure, modelled value migration and a staged, signal-gated pivot — and punishes the five classic errors: over-exploiting the converging core, over-exploring and starving the cash engine, leaving the venture strangled inside the hardware P&L, over-separating it from the installed base and data that were its only edge, and mistiming the pivot. Final KPIs track Profitability (EUR M EBIT vs benchmark), Innovation-Pipeline Value, Organizational Fit, and Adaptation Speed.

You run a EUR 720M industrial-instrumentation unit with a healthy 16% margin — and a converging industry quietly redefining your core. Software-native rivals just took your largest account on subscription analytics. With a EUR 60M envelope and two quarters, balance exploit and explore, redesign the reporting lines, and time the pivot before the window closes.

Round 1 — Read the convergence

Your Decisions This Round

Assumed convergence speed: 40
Two more reference accounts are already evaluating the same competitor, and hardware margin erodes 2–3 points a year. Diagnose the pace honestly — under-read it and the rest of your plan is set to the wrong clock.
Exploit — hardware cost-down, margin defence, calibration-service growth (near-term profit, organizational fit)
Explore — build the analytics/predictive-maintenance platform (high pipeline value, slow, costly)
Explore — acquire a small software firm / hire software talent (fast capability, integration risk)
Envelope allocated: 60 / €60M
Incentive redesign for the venture: 40
Subscription-revenue target in 2 years: 20%
Hardware customers don't rebuy on that cycle and the salesforce is paid on hardware. Signal decline before the subscription revenue exists and you punish the share price; move too slowly and rivals lock in the installed base.
Facilitator (the group CEO & board)
You have two quarters and EUR 60M. Every euro and every hour of senior attention you spend defending the core is unavailable to build the future — adaptation is rivalrous with exploitation, not additive to it. Don't just pick a strategy; remember that the structure often decides whether your exploration survives the gravitational pull of the core. Convince me you have read where value is migrating, and that you have timed the pivot to the window — not to a slide.
